First, I'll parse the SVG path data. The commands are:

- M 83.17,32.03 → Move to starting point
- L 87.90,19.01 → Line to point
- L 76.80,8.19 → Line to point
- L 69.67,12.38 → Line to point
- L 72.92,22.11 → Line to point
- M 72.92,22.11 → Move to new point (this breaks the path into two segments)
- L 83.17,32.03 → Line to point

So the first segment has 5 points: (83.17,32.03), (87.90,19.01), (76.80,8.19), (69.67,12.38), (72.92,22.11) — that's 5 vertices, forming a pentagon.

The second segment is just a line from (72.92,22.11) to (83.17,32.03), which is one of the edges of the pentagon (connecting the last point back to the first point).

So overall, the path draws a closed shape with 5 vertices: a pentagon.

Final answer: (G)
